title: How much do you turn?
hook: Walk round a triangle, then a 12-sided shape. Which makes you turn more?

knows: that a full turn is 360 degrees
that a triangle's angles add up to 180 degrees
doesNotKnow: that the turns at the corners of any shape that bulges outward add up to 360 degrees

misconception: More sides means more total turning.
objective: The learner can explain that walking once round a shape that bulges outward turns you through one full turn, 360 degrees, however many corners share it.

claims.text: At each corner of an equal-sided shape with n sides you turn 360° ÷ n: 120° for 3 sides, 90° for 4, 72° for 5, down to 30° for 12.
claims.source: Regular n-gon exterior angle = 360/n. Recomputed in node for n = 3..12; n × 360/n = 360 each (readout rounds the total, turn shown to 0.1°).

claims.text: Walking once round a shape that only bulges outward and facing forward again is one full turn, so the turns at the corners add up to 360°.
claims.source: Exterior angle sum of a convex polygon is 360° (e.g. any school geometry text; follows from interior sum (n - 2) × 180 since each exterior = 180 - interior). The reveal states it for all convex shapes, beyond the regular ones on stage.

claims.text: Gathered at one point, the n turns close into exactly one circle.
claims.source: n wedges of 360/n placed side by side span 360°. The stage draws them from the same corner angles it draws at the vertices.

recall.question: A robot drives round a six-sided field (any shape that bulges outward) and ends facing the way it started. How far has it turned in total?
options: It depends on the field's shape
recall.why: Going round once and facing forward again is one full spin, 360°, however the turning is shared out between the corners.
